key_insight: The paper splits a kinetic distribution into a wave part determined by local equilibrium over a kinetic horizon and a particle remainder, yielding a continuous bridge from full kinetic transport to Navier–Stokes behavior.
engineering_relevance: This gives a multiscale solver framework that can adapt cell by cell, preserve conservation, and accelerate steady-flow computation in regimes spanning rarefied to near-continuum transport.
method: Define a wave as the equilibrium integral along characteristics over a local kinetic horizon.
Define the particle as the exact complement; wave and particle each satisfy kinetic equations whose moments extend Navier–Stokes.
Use a coupled iteration: macroscopic solve for conservative variables with particle frozen, then kinetic solve for particle with wave fixed.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on hypersonic flow past a cylinder and around the 3D X38 vehicle, showing adaptive wave-particle splitting and strong iteration acceleration.
watch_item: The method depends on choosing and resolving the local horizon-to-relaxation ratio correctly, which may be implementation-sensitive in highly nonuniform flows.
paper_title: A wave-particle decomposition framework for multiscale kinetic transport: continuous-spectrum equations and coupled wave-particle iteration
